advice: Recommend a tail-alignment experiment for the general-size SME fallback: keep the existing predicated row and column tails, but use unpredicated loads only for full 2VL tiles and add a separate edge-tile path with predicates derived from the actual remaining rows and columns. For loads, use valid in-bounds base pointers even when a predicate masks lanes; for stores, predicate every valid output lane. Leave n=512 and its measured assembly unchanged. This is a distinct, legal general-size source change. Hypothesis: removing repeated tail predicates from interior tiles may reduce overhead when dimensions are not multiples of 2VL; benefit is unverified. Check sizes below, equal to, and just above VL and 2VL; odd sizes and tails on each edge; n<=0; finite outputs, .002 tolerance, full overwrite, unchanged inputs, and guards around A, B, and C. Use fresh inputs and compare the complete changed source against same-mode controls under the existing ten-run gates.
risks: The existing code may already handle tails correctly, so this change may add complexity without reducing meaningful work. Edge-path pointer or predicate errors could cause out-of-bounds access or skipped stores. Keep masked load addresses in bounds and do not benchmark or claim a gain before validation.
